01 Antidepressants · class card

SNRIs

serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors · venlafaxine · desvenlafaxine · duloxetine · levomilnacipran · milnacipran

Key point
  • Serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake blocked dose-dependent hypertension, the most common adverse effect of serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs); venlafaxine is typically avoided in hypertension
  • Abrupt stop, most of all with short half-life venlafaxine flu-like discontinuation symptoms within days, without seizures; a slow taper prevents them
  • First line, with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), for generalized anxiety, panic, social anxiety and posttraumatic stress disorders; duloxetine also treats diabetic neuropathy and fibromyalgia
  • With a monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI), linezolid or another serotonergic drug serotonin syndrome
Drugs

Venlafaxine Effexor XR (extended release): short half-life, so more discontinuation symptoms

Desvenlafaxine Pristiq: the active metabolite of venlafaxine

Duloxetine: like venlafaxine in benefit and adverse effects; also treats pain

Levomilnacipran Fetzima

Milnacipran Savella: fibromyalgia

Mechanism

Serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake blocked at the presynaptic neuron

More norepinephrine blood pressure up, dose-dependent

Short half-life (venlafaxine) abrupt stop discontinuation symptoms

Uses

Depression: an alternative to SSRIs

Generalized anxiety, panic and social anxiety disorders: first line with SSRIs

Posttraumatic stress disorder: first line with SSRIs

Obsessive-compulsive disorder: venlafaxine is second line

Duloxetine: diabetic neuropathy, fibromyalgia (milnacipran too); may help chronic low back pain still present after exercise and acetaminophen or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs Neuropathic painFor neuropathic pain, tricyclics or gabapentinoids come first; duloxetine is an option.

Adverse effects

Hypertension, dose-dependent: the most common SNRI adverse effect; block below

Nausea, mostly in the first 2 weeks; also stimulant effects or sedation

Sexual dysfunction, as with SSRIs

Discontinuation syndrome after an abrupt stop, without seizures; block below Discontinuation mnemonicFlu-like symptoms, insomnia, nausea, imbalance, sensory disturbances, hyperarousal: the initials spell "finish"

Serotonin syndrome with another serotonergic drug; block below

Other

Venlafaxine may give a false-positive phencyclidine (PCP) result on a standard urine drug screen

Dose-dependent hypertensionBlood pressure up, more at higher doses; heart rate may rise too

If hypertension is present before starting, choose an antidepressant other than venlafaxine.

Discontinuation syndromeFlu-like aches, dizziness, nausea, irritability or electric shock-like sensations within days of an abrupt stop

Symptoms after an abrupt stop are discontinuation, not relapse or influenza; a patient willing to restart venlafaxine restarts it, then tapers slowly, as the board teaches for paroxetine, another short half-life drug; a patient who will not restart venlafaxine: .

If venlafaxine is to be stopped, choose a slow taper.

Serotonin syndromeTypically fever, mental status changes, autonomic instability, hyperreflexia and clonus after, for example, an MAOI, linezolid, tramadol, a triptan or ondansetron joins an SNRI
Interactions, by result
Combined withResultRule
An MAOI, or linezolid (a weak MAOI)Serotonin syndromeNever together; washout as on the MAOIs card
Tramadol, meperidine, dextromethorphan, triptans, ondansetronSerotonin syndromeRisk adds up; watch for clonus and fever

Practice
  1. 52-year-old man with generalized anxiety disorder at a follow-up visit venlafaxine dose doubled 2 months ago; trazodone at bedtime no new drugs, salt or alcohol change BP 154/98 mm Hg, was 126/80 · HR 92/min → Venlafaxine → venlafaxine raises blood pressure in a dose-dependent way and is typically avoided in hypertension; trazodone blocks alpha-1 receptors and lowers blood pressure on standing
  2. 34-year-old woman stopped venlafaxine abruptly 2 days ago felt well for a year; ran out of pills now dizzy, nauseated, irritable, achy as if with flu T 37.0 °C · no seizures → Restart venlafaxine, then taper slowly → abrupt stops of venlafaxine, a short half-life drug, bring discontinuation symptoms within days, flu-like among them; restarting and tapering slowly treats them
  3. 29-year-old woman with generalized anxiety disorder has a pre-employment urine drug screen takes only venlafaxine; denies any drug use screen positive for phencyclidine calm, oriented · no nystagmus · BP 118/76 mm Hg → Venlafaxine cross-reactivity → venlafaxine can produce a false-positive phencyclidine result on a standard urine drug screen; she has none of the agitation or nystagmus of real use
